notes.title: Patch #6: Faster Unlocks, Smoother Play
notes.content: [p]Patch #6 is here with a focus on smoother gameplay and faster progression. [b]All common cards, guides, and islands are now unlocked by default[/b], and the total bell cost to unlock everything else has been nearly cut in half. I have also made a few balance tweaks, added a quality-of-life improvement for card selection, and dealt with some bugs that have been haunting the game for a tad bit too long.[/p][p][url="https://shows.acast.com/670c223adf4dd6f896322012/68b776d5b4b4b9b3d2aade09"]Shoutout to RoguePod LiteCast for their latest episode, featuring [i]Flocking Hell[/i]![/url] It's a must-listen if you're a fan of [i]Flocking Hell[/i], or curious about game design. Danny & David raise many excellent point, some of which I address in this patch.[/p][p][/p][h3]Full Change Log[/h3][p][b]Quality of Life[/b][/p][list][*][p]If the player has a card selected but clicks on a non-city tile, the card selection is removed and no action happens.[/p][/*][*][p]ALL COMMON cards, guides, and islands now start unlocked! Additionally, many rare cards, guides, and islands now start unlocked.[/p][/*][*][p]Content will now unlock much faster. Unlocking all of the cards, guides, and islands now requires 195 bells (previously 350).[/p][/*][/list][p][b]Cards[/b][/p][list][*][p]Expansive Symbiosis \[4] (common), SIZE gained reduced to 7 (previously 8).[/p][/*][*][p]Gembound Tradition \[3] (rare), CRYSTAL gained increased to 12 (previously 10).[/p][/*][*][p]Hearthbound Tradition \[3] (rare), SIZE gained increased to 10 (previously 8).[/p][/*][*][p]Joint Discovery, now costs 6 and is rare (previously 3 and common). Now gains SHEEP for revealed tiles (previously did not gain SHEEP).[/p][/*][*][p]Secluded Lighthouse (common), now costs 5 (previously 3). Now gains SHEEP for revealed tiles (previously did not gain SHEEP).[/p][/*][*][p]Shining Symbiosis \[4] (common), CRYSTAL gained reduced to 8 (previously 10).[/p][/*][/list][p][b]Bug Fixes[/b][/p][list][*][p]Fixed a bug where some islands that were supposed to have observatories had no special buildings instead.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an exploit where the player could play a card then save + exit the game to inflate the card played and tradition played counters (for cards like Woolbound Tradition).[/p][/*][*][p]Capital City: The Capital City will always be attacked first by the demons, even if another city is closer to the Hell Gate or there is an equidistant city with lower size.[/p][/*][*][p]Hare Trigger: Snarebunnies now have correct legion size even if all turns end with some Snarebunny Invasion triggers remaining.[/p][/*][/list]

notes.title: Patch #5: 16 (!!) New Guides, 5 New Cards, 7 New Islands. My Biggest Update Yet!
notes.content:
I’m thrilled to be part of this week’s [url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wu9qbxNlphA]#TurnBasedThursdayFest on Steam[/url]! It’s a great opportunity to explore turn-based gems, [i]Flocking Hell[/i] included, and enjoy some discounts while you're at it. Go check it out!

Today also marks my [b]largest update to date[/b]! Here’s what’s new in Patch #5:

[list]
[*]16 brand-new Guides: These powerful new guides are companions to existing common guides. They only appear if you’ve already recruited their counterpart, effectively buffing your early-game picks and adding new interesting decisions.
[*]7 challenging new islands, each with a unique mechanic.
[*]5 new cards to unlock new synergies.
[*]And as always, quality-of-life upgrades and bug fixes.
[/list]

Thank you for supporting [i]Flocking Hell[/i]! Whether you're diving in for the first time or returning to test your mettle, there's never been a better moment to play.

[h3]Full Change Log[/h3]

[b]Gameplay[/b]
[list]
[*]When the demons reach the first city, all remaining [SHEEP] will be added to that city as [SIZE].
[/list]

[b]Quality of Life[/b]
[list]
[*]Guides now have a tooltip for any connected mechanics (for example, Tinker now shows the Engineer and Scribe charms in its tooltip).
[*]Cities that are also Teleportation Pools now have a larger, clearer icon. The icon fades out if the city is razed.
[/list]

[b]Charms[/b]
[list]
[*]Planner Charm, new charm: “When you build a road, reveal all adjacent tiles.”
[*]Prophecy Charm, new charm: “Complete the prophecy before the charm expires to receive a reward.”

[list]

[*]Secret Knowledge (common), now costs 3, new text: “Upgrade a random starter card in your deck or discard. (Until the end of the level.)”
[*]Surge [5] (rare), new card: “Gain 30 [CRYSTAL]. If you have less than 85 [CRYSTAL], set your [CRYSTAL] to 85.”
[*]Wool Reserve [5] (rare), new card: “Gain 7 [SHEEP] at the beginning of next island.”

[b]Guides[/b]
[list]
[*]Archeologist 2 (common), new guide: “Beacons provide +0.5 [STRENGTH]. When you activate an observatory, gain 3 [SHEEP]. The growth of cities connected to a teleportation pool is increased by +25%. (Required Guide: Archeologist.)”
[*]Architect 2 (common), new guide: “Every island has an additional city. Cities can appear closer to each other. (Required Guide: Architect.)”
[*]Engineer 2 (common), new guide: “When you connect a city, get the Engineer Charm and the Planner Charm for 1 turn. (Required Guide: Engineer.)”
[*]Explorer 2 (common), new guide: “On turns 40, 30, and 20, equally distribute 90 [SIZE] between all revealed cities. (Required Guide: Explorer.)”

notes.title: Patch #4 Hot Fix: Oops, Double Crystals
notes.content:
No good deed goes unpunished, and no patch comes without a few unexpected bugs!

While developing Competitive², I tested an alternative crystal modifier where all crystal gain (including from cards) was reduced by 25%. Playtesters agreed this felt too harsh, so I removed it. However, in the process, I accidentally doubled crystal production for all difficulty levels. That’s now been fixed, and I hope y'all enjoyed the turbo-charged crystals while they lasted 😅

I also fixed a bug that could cause crashes on some Observatory levels.

[list]
[*]Fixed a bug where [CRYSTAL] production was doubled.
[*]Fixed a bug where the game would rarely crash when starting an island with observatories.
[/list]

notes.title: Patch #4: Hopping and More Dangerous Than Ever
notes.content:
Thank you all for continuing to play, share, and enjoy [i]Flocking Hell[/i]! It’s been amazing to see so many of you take the mantle of the Bellwether and lead the flock against the demons. Patch #4 brings some major updates to keep things fresh and challenging. Snarebunnies are back and sneakier than ever with the brand new [b]Hare Trigger[/b] island. To celebrate the occasion, our composer Simon Daoud wrote a new track, [b]Meat the End[/b]! Combat now flows faster thanks to improved animations and dynamic damage stacking. Full details below, with the change log at the end of the post.

Before we begin, a HUGE shout-out to Draham, our new German community translator. Draham volunteered to review and polish the German translation of [i]Flocking Hell[/i], making the game more accessible in the process. Thanks Draham 💜

[h3]A Hare-y Situation[/h3]

This patch introduces the second Snarebunny bonus level, [b]Hare Trigger[/b], along with its prelude, [b]Nose for Trouble[/b]! Once again, you’ll face multiple waves of Snarebunnies, but this time their arrival depends on how you spend your turns. Every decision matters!

To celebrate, our amazing composer Simon Daoud created a brand new boss battle track: [b]Meat the End[/b]. You’ll hear it in every boss fight from now on! Be sure to [url=https://www.instagram.com/simondaoudmusic/]check out Simon’s Instagram[/url] for more of his wonderful music, and remember that you can buy the OST through Steam.

[h3]Reinforcing Reinforcements[/h3]

Since launch, "go-wide" strategies (where you connect as many cities as possible) have lagged behind. Roads are expensive, and late connections suffer from diminishing returns. This patch gives them a major boost: reinforcements no longer reduce the size of reinforcing cities. For example, connecting 10 cities will gain a total of 225 size across all cities when the demons invade!

Two other changes also support going wide. First, demon legion size is now pre-calculated, removing a hidden penalty that punished large city networks. Second, all islands now spawn with exactly 12 cities (instead of 10–12), making cities closer together and synergy cards like [b]Oracle[/b] easier to trigger.

[h3]Faster Combat[/h3]

Combat just got a lot snappier! First, I trimmed delays from key animations, including the "Reinforcements!" prompt, to keep things moving. Second, I added dynamic stacking to the damage multiplier. When large armies clash, up to 32 sheep attacks and demon swipes are now combined into a single animation. Battles are still fun to watch and now take about half the time.

[h3]Demon Attack Order[/h3]

You can now mouse over the Hell Gate to see the order in which the demon legion will attack your cities. Keep in mind that this order can change: as cities grow, demons will prefer smaller cities when distances are equal. For some bosses (like the Butchers), only the first city is guaranteed, and the rest are decided as combat unfolds.

[h3]Multiplicative Cards Rarity Changes[/h3]

Multiplicative effects are very popular right now. Two excellent examples are Balatro and Ballionaire, where the goal is to reach millions or billions of total points. [i]Flocking Hell[/i] takes a different approach, focusing on small, important decisions and gradual growth.

That said, two cards ([b]Crystalline Seed[/b] and [b]Ritual of Growth[/b]) and the [b]Geologist[/b] guide break this rule and can lead to runaway wins if drafted and stacked. To keep them exciting but make them less common, I’ve increased their rarities from rare to epic.

[h3]New Content![/h3]

No patch is complete without fresh content! Alongside [b]Hare Trigger[/b], this update adds [b]Tainted Quarry[/b], a new island that puts small-deck strategies to the test, and two new Tradition cards that grow stronger as your campaign progresses.

Enough reading! Now go play 🐑😈

[h3]Full Change Log[/h3]
[list]
[*]Flocking Hell now has an updated German translation, thanks to Draham, our new community translator! If you’d like to help with any of the other languages, please email us at anna@sextantstudios.games.
[*]Check out the new boss battle music, [b]Meat the End[/b]! Kudos to Simon Daoud, Flocking Hell’s talented composer, for creating this new track.
[/list]
[h3]Quality of Life[/h3]
[list]
[*]Mouse over the revealed, active Hell Gate to see the current order in which the demons will attack your cities (it can change as you reveal more cities and as cities grow in size!).
[*]The combat at each city will take less swipes thanks to a new dynamic stacking damage multiplier, making combat faster
[*]Shortened several combat animations (such as the “Reinforcements!” prompt and the raze animation wait), making combat faster
[/list]
[h3]Gameplay[/h3]
[list]
[*]Demon legion [SIZE] is pre-calculated (previously calculated based on total starting city size). This should make Competitive and Competitive² harder!
[*]Each island will now have 12 cities (previously it was 10-12).
[*]Reinforcements now gain +5 [SIZE] for each connected city, but do not cost any [SIZE] for the reinforcing cities.
[*]Competitive and Competitive²: The first Snarebunny wave will now have 125 [DEMONSIZE] (previously 100).
[*]Competitive²: Demon legion is now larger than Competitive, and grows faster.
[/list]
[h3]Cards[/h3]
[list]
[*]Crystalline Seed [4], now epic (previously rare).
[*]Gembound Tradition [3] (rare), new card: “Gain 10 [CRYSTAL] for each time you played “Gembound Tradition” this campaign.”
[*]Hearthbound Tradition [3] (rare), new card: “This city gains +8 [SIZE] for each time you played “Hearthbound Tradition” this campaign.”
[*]Ritual of Growth [3], now epic (previously rare).
[/list]
[h3]Guides[/h3]
[list]
[*]Geologist, now epic (previously rare).
[/list]
[h3]Islands[/h3]
[list]
[*]Emberfrost Expanse (late-game), will now have 10 cities (previously 8), and they are no longer especially distant from each other.
[*]Hare Trigger (boss), new island: “The Snarebunnies attack whenever the Invasion Charm gets to 0! The charm drops by 5 whenever you assign to a mine, build a road, or play a card. (It does not tick down when you reveal a tile.) There are at most 4 waves. Until the last wave, your Crystal Blast only uses half your [CRYSTAL].”
[*]Nose for Trouble (late-game), new island: “There are 4 Hell Gates, located all over the island. One is active and the rest are dormant. Whenever you assign to a mine, build a road, or play a card, the active Hell Gate changes. Build a road on a dormant Hell Gate to close it.”
[*]Rumor Mill (late-game), playing the fourth “Fake News” card will reveal 8 random tiles (previously 10).
[*]Tainted Quarry (late-game), new island: “When you fortify a city, gain 1 [SHEEP]. Whenever your deck runs out of cards, add a Curse to your deck at the start of the next level.”
[/list]
[h3]Bug Fixes[/h3]
[list]
[*]Hopefully fixed a bug where a player would lose the campaign but still kept going despite having 0 hearts left.
[*]The Scribe Charm will now correctly say “Scribe” in the UI (instead of “Clerk”).
[*]Fixed a bug where the Cartographer guide will sometimes crash a new island.
[*]City growth pop-up font color is now using the correct shade of green
[/list]

notes.title: Patch #3: Patch Squared
notes.content:
[i]Flocking Hell[/i] keeps growing, and I couldn’t be happier to welcome so many new players to the flock! Thank you for the love and feedback 💜 This patch brings exciting updates: a new difficulty mode for the bold, better chances at epic cards, two new crystal-focused islands, and a few balance tweaks to keep the game fresh.

(As always, the full change log is below.)

[h3]New Difficult Level: Competitive²[/h3]

Full disclosure: my personal win rate on Competitive is around 40%. But based on your feedback, some of you are way ahead of me! A few brave souls even asked for a harder mode, so here it is.

In Competitive², your crystal production is reduced by 25% and imps start with +0.5 strength. Think you’ve mastered [i]Flocking Hell[/i]? Time to prove it! 🐑😈😈😈

[h3]Higher Epic Drop Rate[/h3]

Epics are some of the most powerful and flavorful cards and guides in [i]Flocking Hell[/i], and in my opinion, among the most fun. But their strength means they can occasionally trivialize a run. Because of their rarity, I spend relatively little time balancing epics. If you find one that fits your build, your odds of winning go up significantly. That’s by design. They balance mayhem by their rarity.

However, I feel epics are a bit too rare at the moment. So in this patch, I’m slightly increasing their appearance rate. Previously, rare cards had a 5% chance to convert into an epic. That chance is now 7.5%.

[h3]Stronger Tunneler[/h3]

[b]Tunneler[/b] is the first rare guide that I designed. I was showcasing the game to designer friends and wanted something fun that breaks the game rules in an interesting way. [b]Tunneler[/b] was a great fit, and it’s still one of my favorite guides. However, it’s clear that it’s weaker than other rare guides that were developed later in the design process (such as [b]Potholer[/b], which has a similar role). Therefore, I’m giving [b]Tunneler[/b] a hefty buff, increasing the crystal gain and adding a tile reveal to every road build.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45234997/e5672a25e506c64c6ec1f2663a080d14834036aa.png[/img]

[h3]New Crystal-Focused Islands[/h3]

This patch adds two new islands with unique twists on crystal production. [b]Roots of Industry[/b] starts with –25% crystal production, but you can boost it by connecting fortified cities. [b]Veinbound[/b] makes all mines start with –10 max size (meaning you can’t assign sheep at first), but rewards you with free mine size as you connect cities. Both islands encourage hybrid strategies that blend mining and city building.

Related to this, some playtesters noted that many existing islands (like [b]Jealousy[/b]) interfere with [i]Flocking Hell[/i]’s core city-connection gameplay. Moving forward, expect more islands that support your building efforts, not just complicate them.

[h3]Nerfs to Card Cost Reductions[/h3]

I really don’t like nerfs.

Nerfs are often used in multiplayer games to address frustrating or overpowered mechanics. Neither of these arguments is relevant for [i]Flocking Hell[/i], a single-player roguelite where every campaign has its own “meta”.

However, after much consideration, I decided to nerf [b]Charming Ritual III[/b], [b]Comptroller[/b], and [b]Scribe[/b] (which is now named [b]Clerk[/b]). All three provide consistent, predictable reductions to card costs, which creates two major design problems:

One, they make it difficult to design new cost-reduction mechanics. For example, [b]Mason[/b] and [b]Tinker[/b] often feel underwhelming by comparison to [b]Comptroller[/b] and [b]Scribe[/b]. Every new discount guide ends up being measured against these two, which limits creativity.

Two, they skew how I evaluate every new card. When I buffed city size cards in Patch #1, I had to balance them for both [b]Scribe[/b] builds and non-[b]Scribe[/b] builds. That added complexity complicates playtesting, slows down development, and restricts card design.

The end result is that [b]Charming Ritual III[/b], [b]Comptroller[/b], and [b]Scribe[/b] limit future design space and make it harder to introduce fun new options. My goal with these nerfs is to keep them strong and enjoyable, while giving the rest of the game more room to grow.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45234997/9c899103f6cbe42805339cc9852e1aedded8f584.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45234997/8b49a18d9f6fac697d63dcb76b4f4cbc5197fa8d.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45234997/d9ed5a2e90d513804b2c40476f047d42744d8efc.png[/img]

[h3]Full Change Log[/h3]

[b]New difficulty level: Competitive²![/b]
[list]
[*] [CRYSTAL] production decreased by 25%.
[*] Imps spawn with +0.5 [STRENGTH].
[/list]
[b]Campaign[/b]
[list]
[*] The chance of a rare converting into an epic is now 7.5% (previously 5%)
[/list]
[b]Cards[/b]
[list]
[*] Charming Ritual III [2] (special), now gains the Scribe charm for 6 turns (previously 9 turns).
[/list]
[b]Guides[/b]
[list]
[*] Comptroller (rare), ability updated: “Building a road and assigning to a mine cost 1 less [SHEEP]. City growth and mine production reduced by 15%.” (previously “All actions cost 1 less [SHEEP]. City growth and mine production reduced by 25%”).
[*] Scribe (rare), now says “Playing common cards costs 1 less [SHEEP].” (previously “Playing a card”).
[*] Tunneler (rare), building a road through a mountain will now gain 30 crystals (previously 20 crystals) and will also reveal all adjacent non-mountain tiles.
[/list]
[b]Islands[/b]
[list]
[*] Emberfrost Expanse (late-game), slightly reduced the minimum distance between cities (from 3.5 to 3.25) and updated the description to “at most 8 cities”.
[*] Roots of Industry (early-game), new island: “Crystal Mines produce -25% [CRYSTAL]. Crystal Mines produce +10% [CRYSTAL] for each connected, fortified city.”
[*] Veinbound (late-game), new island: “Decrease the maximum size of all mine by 10.
When you connect one or more new cities, the nearest mine is marked and gains 5 size.”
[/list]
[b]Bug Fixes[/b]
[list]
[*] The starting tile can no longer be on a farm or adjacent to the Hell Gate.
[*] Pioneers+ now correctly reveals a pasture next to an unrevealed city (as opposed to a pasture next to a revealed city).
[/list]

notes.title: Patch #2 Hotfix: Simplified Chinese, Japanese, and Korean Support

notes.title: Patch #2: Go Wide, Grow Strong, Stand Tall!
notes.content:
Thanks for all the love you’ve shown Flocking Hell since launch! I'm excited by all the new players who have joined our flock. Remember that you can find us on Bluesky and Discord, links are below.

I’m committed to regular updates and listening closely to your feedback. Patch #2 focuses on making city-based strategies more powerful, flexible, and fun. Below, I’ll walk you through the thinking behind the latest changes. The full change log is right after my notes.

[h3]City Size Buff[/h3]

[i]Flocking Hell[/i] offers two main ways to fight the demons: collecting crystals for the Crystal Blast, or growing your cities. Both are supported by the map (mines for crystals, roads for city growth) and amplified by cards and guides.

Crystals are straightforward: 30 crystals = +30 damage. City Size, however, is less direct. The demon legion gains +0.5 Strength for every city it razes, which makes early cities near the Hell Gate more valuable than distant ones. That means city-based strategies are more sensitive to when and where you find the Hell Gate.

Since launch, several players have voiced frustration with city builds. After reviewing the numbers, I agree: city Size cards were tuned around finding the Hell Gate early and playing them close to it. But in practice, that’s not always possible, especially when you also need to gather sheep and build roads.

Therefore, I buffed all city Size cards. Finding the Hell Gate early is still helpful, but now city strategies should feel more viable even if you get a slower start.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45234997/774438cfb5b3e56dd4ba4e102d33c7d5990ac1df.png[/img]

[h3]Witching Hour[/h3]

On that note, I buffed [b]Witching Hour[/b] to reveal the Cottage instead of marking it. While [b]Witching Hour[/b] is easy to trigger, there’s no guarantee that candidate cities will be near the Hell Gate. The card gains a free turn with this buff, so I hope it will entice players to pick it more often despite its positional limitation.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45234997/1aad76740e8e9b263f037f73eed5cf45cb0f90e1.png[/img]

[h3]More Attention to Strength and Going Wide[/h3]

At its core, [i]Flocking Hell[/i] was always designed to revolve around cities. Cards open up alternative strategies, like stacking crystals or building one enormous city, but I feel that the foundational gameplay of connecting cities hasn’t gotten enough love with cards and guides. So, this patch buffs several mechanics that encourage you to go wide.

First, I want to highlight Strength as a way to power up cities. Cities with higher Strength are more effective against the demons, even when they’re far from the Hell Gate. As a starting point, [b]Population Boom[/b] now grants Strength instead of Size, and [b]Heavy Walls[/b] gives a larger one-time Strength boost. If players find this impactful and fun, future patches may explore more Strength-based tools.

I’ve also buffed a few key “go-wide” enablers: [b]Common Roots[/b] is now 1 sheep cheaper, and both [b]Innkeeper[/b] and [b]Surveyor[/b] gain 20 Size instead of 15. Together, these changes should make wide strategies more tempting AND more powerful!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45234997/3796f3548cfb6b6aa17167355f672215c93bbcb0.png[/img]

[h3]Island Changes[/h3]

Lastly, I’ve made tweaks to three islands:

[b]The Butcher’s Wake[/b] and [b]The Feast[/b] now have clearer text to better explain their mechanics. This is especially important since they appear in the tutorial and have been confusing newcomers.

For [b]Embers of Defiance[/b], I reduced the number of BBQs from 5 to 3. Losing 25 sheep felt too punishing. Three BBQs should preserve the core dilemma of the island while reducing frustration.

[b]Thank you for reading![/b] Now ... go play 🐑😈

[h3]Full Change Log[/h3]

[b]Cards[/b]
[list]
[*]Advance Warning [3] (common), now gains +35 [SIZE] (previously +30 [SIZE]
[*]Common Roots (common), cost reduced to 4 (previously 5)
[*]Expedition Log [3] (common), now gains +20 [SIZE] (previously +15 [SIZE])
[*]Heavy Walls [5] (common), new ability: “If this is the first time you play Heavy Walls on this city, it gains +1 [STRENGTH].” (previously “This city gains +0.5 [STRENGTH].”)

notes.title: First patch, OST now available, and a Shoutout from Olexa!
notes.content:
What an incredible first week! I’m beyond grateful to everyone who picked up [i]Flocking Hell[/i], joined the Discord, shared your reviews & kind words, and ... reported bugs. Your excitement and feedback have meant the world, and helped us push out our first patch that much faster. Thank you for being part of the flock!

I would like to especially thank Olexa, a leading indie YouTuber, for introducing [i]Flocking Hell[/i] to his viewers! You can find the full video here:

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_VjnExgb7So

Olexa kindly summarized his review with "[[i]Flocking Hell[/i] is] a fascinating little game that is fun to pick up and play. I like it a lot, easy to play, difficult to master, filled with a bunch of content."

[h2]Official Soundtrack Now Available[/h2]

The official [i]Flocking Hell[/i] soundtrack is now available for purchase on Steam! Huge thanks to the incredibly talented Simon Daoud, who composed the entire OST and brought so much atmosphere to the game. All proceeds from the soundtrack go directly to Simon: support the music, support the composer!

[h2]2025-04-01 Patch Notes[/h2]

I'm especially excited to announce our first patch! For this release, we addressed several bugs that were reported by players over the past week, made a couple of small balance changes, and introduced a pop-up whenever you unlock a new island. We have big plans for [i]Flocking Hell[/i], and hope to announce regular content updates in the coming weeks.

[list]
[*]All bell requirements have been reduced. Unlocking new content is now faster.
[*]When a new island is unlocked, a pop-up screen will appear during the main menu.
[/list]
[b]Quality of Life[/b]
[list]
[*] Islands in the codex “Islands” tab will now show their unlock bell requirement.
[/list]
[b]Gameplay[/b]
[list]
[*] The starting deck will always include either [b]Map to Riches[/b] or [b]Map to the Cities[/b].
[/list]
[b]Cards[/b]
[list]
[*] [b]Pioneers[/b] [3] (starter), will no longer reveal pastures adjacent to the city where you played the card.
[*] [b]Vast Meadows[/b] [3] (common), now has reminder text with the number of turns the charm will be gained for.
[*] [b]Verdant Force[/b] [3] (common), rewritten as “All hidden adjacent pastures become small farms.” (while this is a minor nerf, it is similar functionality in most cases and simpler for newcomers).
[/list]
[b]Islands[/b]
[list]
[*] [b]Tiny Towns[/b] (late-game), starting city SIZE is now reduced by 10% (previously 25%).
[/list]
[b]Bug Fixes[/b]
[list]
[*] Sheep will no longer walk all over the codex when opening it during a level.
[*] Tutorial: The tutorial now correctly indicates that the “View Deck” button is in the top right.
[*] Corrupted Cacophony: The island will now correctly start with start-of-level effects, such as Cartographer and Foreman.
[*] Fluffocalypse: The island description should no longer overflow.
[*] The “No Mutton for You” achievement should now trigger correctly on both The Feast and Buffer of Horrors.
[/list]
Lastly, the demo has been updated to the latest version of the game, including all bug fixes and interface updates (locked content is still locked, though!)

notes.title: Flocking Hell demo update!
notes.content:
WAKE UP SHEEPLE! There's a new version of the [i]Flocking Hell[/i] demo, in preparation for the upcoming Steam Next Fest. The focus for this release is quality-of-life improvements, including:

[*] A new "View Map" button that allows you to survey your island once a level is complete
[*] Redesigned progression and unlocks
[*] Clearer text for most of the cards and guides

Of course, a patch is also a great opportunity for new content, and this one introduces the Observatory! We originally planned to make this building full game-only, but it's so fun, we decided to include it in the demo as well.

notes.title: The new Flocking Hell demo is OUT!
notes.content:
WAKE UP SHEEPLE! We’re thrilled to announce the release of the new [i]Flocking Hell[/i] demo. After months of hard work and incorporating invaluable feedback from our amazing playtesters and demo players, the game is now better than ever.

There have been too many changes to list in this one post (the change log is over 10 pages!) Every game system has been redesigned from the ground up, including:
[list]
[*] City growth
[*] Crystals
[*] Playing and drafting cards
[*] Combat
[*] and much more!
[/list]
[i]Flocking Hell[/i] is now more strategic, more transparent, and much more fun! Go check it out, and don't forget to wishlist ahead of the full release in late March 🐑😈

notes.title: 24 hours of Flocking Hell: Thank you! + First Patch
notes.content:
Wow, what an incredible first day! Thank you to everyone who downloaded the demo, played, and shared your feedback. Your ideas and suggestions are amazing, and I’m committed to implementing the best ones to make [i]Flocking Hell[/i] even better. Check out the latest patch notes at the end of this announcement.

If you spot a bug or have more ideas, feel free to hop into our Discord channel or use the feedback form on the game’s main menu.

It’s been a joy seeing your positive responses on Bluesky, YouTube, and Discord. Keep them coming, and enjoy the game!

-- Elli (they/them)
